subject: Hosted API renewal — stepped monthly commit + rate-band sync
messages:
From: Elena Morris <elena.morris@polarisai.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal and new monthly baseline question

Hi Jonas,

We’re coming up on our annual renewal and the execs want to consolidate our hosted usage into a higher guaranteed monthly commit for 12 months. Current pattern: strong growth spikes during model training/experiments in Q4 and heavy inference bursts around marketing campaigns.

High-level ask: can Redwood support a stepped commit that starts at 4M tokens/month for Q3, ramps to 7M in Q4, then 10M for the final 6 months? We’re also concerned about the soft throttle behavior during 24–48hr spikes — want clarity on how burst pockets vs. permanent commit will be handled (and any rate-limit floors during spikes).

Attached: our May usage export for context. Procurement will need a quote and expected invoice cadence (monthly vs. quarterly). Can we get a recommended plan and numbers this week?

Thanks,
Elena Morris
Head of Platform
PolarisAI

Attachment: polaris_usage_may2027.csv (CSV, 62KB)
From: jonas.weber@redwood.com <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morris <elena.morris@polarisai.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, jasmine.liu@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-14T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal and new monthly baseline question

Elena — thanks for the context and the export, that helps. High level response inline and a proposed starter commercial attached.

Summary / quick answer:
- We can support a stepped commit as you described (4M -> 7M -> 10M tokens/month) on a 12-month renewal.
- Billing cadence: standard is monthly invoicing; we can do quarterly invoice cadence for a slight billing admin change (notes below).
- Burst behavior: Redwood’s burst architecture separates temporary burst pockets from committed capacity — short spikes of 24–48 hours will be covered by a burst buffer (configurable), but sustained traffic above the committed band will be metered to the next tier unless you convert burst consumption into committed tokens.

Action items I propose now:
1) I’ll attach a one-page proposal showing the step schedule and the rate bands (see attached proposal_v1.pdf).
2) Karthik (cc’d) will confirm any discount bands for year-over-year growth and provide the formal quote/PO line items.
3) Jasmine (cc’d) will follow up with an ops checklist for onboarding the ramp (KV cache warm-up, recommended prefilling windows for campaign spikes).

Questions for you (short):
- Do you want monthly or quarterly invoices?
- Any internal approval required for changing invoice cadence or seat contacts?

I’ll wait for your answers and will push a formal quote to you today if procurement confirms the invoice cadence.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

Attachment: proposal_v1.pdf (PDF, 18KB)

Date: 2027-06-14T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal and new monthly baseline question

Jonas — appreciated. Quick answers inline below and a couple of clarifications.

> Do you want monthly or quarterly invoices?
We prefer quarterly invoices (finance team request).

> Any internal approval required for changing invoice cadence or seat contacts?
Procurement will sign once we have the final line items and an SLA note around burst handling. I’m adding them here — procure@polarisai.com — please include a PO-ready PDF.

Clarifications:
- For Q4 training spikes, we expect up to 18–24 hour sustained peaks that could exceed committed tokens by ~60% for small windows; we need the soft throttle floor documented (requests/sec per token tier) and a fallback routing plan if the primary region hits capacity.
- Can you include a short ops playbook item for warm cache behavior and recommended batch sizes to avoid latency regressions during campaign bursts?

Thanks — attaching the May export again for reference.

Elena

All — following up with the refined commercial and an ops checklist. Per Elena’s ask we set invoice cadence to quarterly and added a short SLA note on burst behavior and fallback routing. Key bullets below and links to the shared artifacts:

Mutual action plan (summary):
- Week 0: Polaris signs the 12-month agreement for stepped commit (4M / 7M / 10M). DocuSign link included.
- Week 1: Redwood kickoff (Jasmine) — onboarding checklist: KV cache prefilling windows, recommended batching (stateless batch size 8–16), warmup traffic schedule for Q4 training.
- Week 2–4: Prod validation and smoke tests; set up observability dashboards (latency, token burn by route).

Commercial highlights (summary):
- Effective per-token rates by band are in the attached PO-ready PDF. Quarterly invoices will be issued with Net30 terms.
- Burst buffer: up to 20% aggregated burst capacity retained for short spikes; any sustained consumption beyond burst buffer will be billed against the next committed tier unless converted to a permanent commit (we’ve noted this in the SLA section).

Attachments & links: the formal quote (proposal_v1.pdf), the May usage CSV (polaris_usage_may2027.csv), and I’ve created a DocuSign envelope for POL-2027-0539: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/renewal/POL-2027-0539

Please review the DocuSign today if possible and Procurement, if you need the quote in a different format or with a PO field prefilled let me know and Karthik will produce a PO-ready PDF.

Karthik, can you confirm the exact PO line strings we should include (rate per token per band + quarterly invoice SKU)?

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if any of this needs a walkthrough.

Jonas Weber
